correctness.rationale: Directly reconstructed the published cut-vertex identity from independent rate-one departure clocks, Kac/Wald stopped physical lengths, old and new two-leaf local-survival functions and terminal suffix corrections. In the positive remote path, gambler ruin yields exactly Exp(1/q), a=1/(q+1), b=2/(3q+2), J=q^2, and an explicitly positive rational polynomial. In the negative remote stem-plus-terminal-K-clique, a single rate-one remote excursion covers every remote vertex with probability at least 1/[2(r+1)]; this uses a 1/(r+1) gambler-ruin gateway probability and an explicit coupon/bridge-exit bound below 1/2 for all K>=100. Consequently ET<=2(r+1) and E exp(-T)>=1/(2r+3). Nonnegativity of the terminal correction and b<=a give a strictly negative upper bound under K>=4r+10. Marked radius balls, ambient-degree boundary labels and exact graph order are checked algebraically. An independent exact-rational visited-mask Bellman verifier checks three finite examples, including r=2, and independent numerical inequalities on 203 radii; these do not replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Si (arXiv:2608.27474v1) explicitly states this equal-order strengthening as an unresolved open problem (Section 7, item 2); their witness graphs have unequal orders and different remote topology. The construction here proves the strictly stronger equal-order theorem for all r, without claiming the published transfer theorem or generic edge sign-reversal as new. A primary full-text theorem/implication comparison, published-record semantic searches and recoverable own-ledger claim comparisons did not locate covering prior work. Residual unindexed or newly posted equal-order constructions remain possible.

value.rationale: Solves the precise equal-order strengthening listed as open problem 2 by the motivating 2026 paper. Matching n rules out the most conspicuous available global scalar (graph order) from sign inference; the construction works at every prescribed radius, simultaneously preserving degree-labelled local topology, marked distance and electrical resistance. Explicit strict positive formula and strict negative coupon-thinning bound make the obstruction interpretable and reproducible, rather than a finite arbitrary counterexample. No claim is made about optimal graph size, worst-start cover times or polynomial algorithms.
